tasks.definition: The fraction or percentage of incoming radiation reflected by a surface or object.
In genetics, the occurrence of two or more alternative forms of a DNA sequence within a population.
Personal income remaining after personal current taxes, available for spending or saving.
A medical imaging technique that uses high-frequency sound waves and their echoes to form images of structures inside the body.
One of two or more alternative DNA sequences at a particular location in a genome.
In tennis, winning the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open in the same event category within one calendar year.
Malware that blocks access to a system or its data, commonly by encryption, and demands payment to restore access.
The study of the Sun's internal structure and motions by analysing oscillations observed at its surface.
A section of a jet engine that burns additional fuel in the exhaust stream after the turbine to increase thrust.
A sequence of nodes in which each node stores data and a link to the next node, and sometimes also to the previous node.
A medium in which electric current is carried by moving ions, or a substance that produces such ions when dissolved or melted.
A segment within an RNA transcript that is removed during splicing and is absent from the resulting mature RNA.
In cricket, the state in which the ball is no longer in play, so that further action with that ball cannot normally score runs or dismiss a batter.
A reference in a digital document that a user can activate to open another resource or move to another location in the same document.
A semiconductor device used to amplify electrical signals or switch electric current.
A material with high electrical resistance that strongly restricts the flow of electric current and is used to separate conductors.
Goods and services used up in producing other goods and services during an accounting period, excluding fixed assets used repeatedly over time.
The value of an industry's or sector's output minus the goods and services used as intermediate inputs; it measures its contribution to gross domestic product.
The change of a substance from gas to liquid; in weather, water vapour changing into liquid water droplets.
The production of genetically identical or nearly identical copies of a DNA sequence, cell, or organism.
The process by which a cell copies its DNA, producing new DNA molecules from existing DNA templates.
A machine-readable pattern, such as parallel bars or a two-dimensional arrangement of marks, that encodes information for optical scanning.
Hardware or software storage that keeps copies of data so that later requests can be served more quickly.
A controlled heat treatment of food or drink that reduces disease-causing and spoilage microorganisms without necessarily sterilising the product.
An electronic circuit with two interacting switching stages that produces pulses, timed transitions, or two stable states, depending on its configuration.

Produced assets used repeatedly or continuously in production for more than a year, such as buildings, equipment, and intellectual property products; consumer durables are excluded in national accounts.
An experimental method for studying stress in transparent materials by observing stress-induced changes in how they transmit polarised light.
In chess, a position in which the player to move has their king under attack and no legal move can remove the attack; that player loses the game.
A wireless communication technology that uses radio waves to exchange data between nearby compatible devices.
A long, narrow region of the atmosphere that transports large amounts of water vapour, often bringing heavy precipitation when it reaches land.
The average rate of net electrical energy transfer in a circuit, measured in watts; also called real power.
In cricket, an illegal delivery called by an umpire for a specified infringement, such as the bowler overstepping the front crease; it normally awards an extra run and restricts possible dismissals.
The process by which information in a gene is used to produce a functional RNA or protein product.
Heat from within the Earth that can be used for heating or electricity generation.
Dependence of a system's present response on its previous states or inputs, rather than on the current input alone.
A problem-solving technique in which a procedure calls itself on smaller or simpler instances, with a base case that ends the repeated calls.
A gas that undergoes little or no chemical reaction under the specified conditions.
An electrical conductor that provides an interface through which current enters or leaves another medium or device.
A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the resulting heat to a fluid or other medium for use or storage.
A person who undertakes a temporary period of work to gain practical experience in a field or organisation.
Online content whose headline, thumbnail, or description is designed to attract clicks, often through sensationalism or misleading promises.
A paper or digital voucher or code that entitles its holder to a discount or other specified purchase benefit.
A device that amplifies or generates coherent microwave radiation through stimulated emission from excited atoms or molecules.
A member of a class of organic compounds based on a characteristic framework of four fused carbon rings, including many hormones and sterols.
In cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rises towards the batter's upper body or head after bouncing.
An excessive and persistent fear of heights that can cause marked anxiety and avoidance.
An automatic control system that uses feedback to regulate a mechanical variable such as position, speed, or acceleration.
The use of computational methods to store, organise, and analyse biological data, such as DNA sequences, protein sequences, and information about genes.
Describing wind that flows upslope along a hillside or mountain, typically because daytime heating warms the air next to the slope.
An electrical generator that converts mechanical energy into alternating-current electrical energy.
A dark, fine-grained volcanic rock formed when lava relatively low in silica cools rapidly, typically containing plagioclase and pyroxene.
A rotating machine that converts energy from flowing liquid or gas into mechanical power on a shaft.
A family of standards for wired network communication, widely used to connect devices in local area networks.
A small piece of data that a website asks a browser to store and send back with later requests, for purposes such as maintaining a session or remembering preferences.
An imaging technique that reconstructs cross-sectional views of internal structures from measurements that encode information about the inside of an object or body.
The study of the chemical composition of matter in the universe and the processes that produced its elements and compounds.
A digital display that brings together important measurements or status information for monitoring a system, activity, or organisation.
In association football, the scoring of three goals by the same player in one match.
A hospital unit providing specialised care for newborn babies, especially those born prematurely or needing medical treatment.
A resistor whose resistance changes strongly with temperature; depending on its type, the resistance may increase or decrease as temperature rises.
A search method for sorted data that repeatedly compares a target with the middle item of the remaining interval and discards the half that cannot contain it.
An electrical component designed to provide resistance, limiting current or producing a voltage drop and dissipating electrical energy as heat.
The process of finding, investigating, and correcting faults in software or hardware that cause incorrect or unexpected behaviour.
The transformation of readable information into ciphertext using a cryptographic algorithm and a key, so that it can be recovered through authorised decryption.
In cricket, a delivery judged beyond the striker's reach for a normal cricket stroke under the applicable positioning rules; a no-ball takes precedence over a wide.
A collection in which items are added at the rear and removed from the front, so the earliest added item is removed first: first in, first out.
Personal income remaining after personal current taxes and personal outlays, including consumption, interest payments, and current transfers.
A subatomic particle with baryon number +1, such as a proton or neutron; ordinary baryons consist of three quarks.
Energy sources replenished by natural processes on human timescales, such as sunlight, wind, flowing water, biomass, and geothermal heat.
An instrument for measuring electric potential difference between two points.
A substance capable of provoking an allergic reaction in a sensitive person.
A spanning tree of a connected, weighted, undirected graph whose total edge weight is as small as possible.
A decentralised digital currency whose transactions are verified by a peer-to-peer network and recorded on a public blockchain without a central issuing bank.
A tube inserted into the body to introduce or remove fluids, such as delivering medication or draining urine.
A finite sequence of well-defined steps for solving a problem or carrying out a computation.
The production of electricity and useful heat from the same energy source in an integrated process; also called combined heat and power.
The branch of mathematics concerned with vectors, vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and systems of linear equations.
A graph in which every edge has a direction from one vertex to another.
The transfer of heat by the bulk movement of a liquid or gas; in weather, often associated with rising warm air and sinking cooler air.
A transaction that a bank pays despite insufficient funds in the customer's account, causing the account balance to fall below zero.
A hinged control surface near the trailing edge of an aircraft wing, used with the opposite wing's aileron to control rolling motion.
Software or hardware that records keystrokes entered on a keyboard, often covertly to capture sensitive information.
Treatment that stimulates, suppresses, or otherwise modifies immune responses to help treat disease.
Random changes in allele frequencies across generations due to chance sampling in a finite population, with stronger effects in smaller populations.
Automated recognition of individuals using measurable biological or behavioural characteristics, such as fingerprints, facial features, or voice patterns.
A change in wind speed or direction over a horizontal or vertical distance.
The simultaneous purchase and sale of the same or comparable assets in different markets to profit from a price difference.
A small, intense downdraft that spreads out near the ground over less than about four kilometres, producing strong, short-lived winds and wind shear.
A machine in which expanding steam turns a bladed rotor, converting the steam's energy into rotating mechanical power.
A connected subgraph that includes every vertex of an undirected graph and contains no cycles.
A prolonged seasonal state of reduced activity and metabolism, with lowered body temperature and heart rate, that helps certain animals survive cold or food scarcity.
An apparatus in which a nuclear fission chain reaction can be initiated, controlled, and sustained, typically to produce heat or neutrons.
The study of layers of rock or sediment, including their sequence, distribution, relationships, and relative ages.
An instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure.
A vessel or system that maintains controlled conditions for biological reactions involving cells, microorganisms, or enzymes.
A protective region of repetitive DNA and associated proteins at the end of a linear chromosome that helps prevent damage and inappropriate joining of chromosome ends.
A deceptive communication that impersonates a trusted source to trick someone into revealing sensitive information, transferring money, or taking an unsafe action.
A line on a weather map joining locations with equal atmospheric pressure.
In an alternating-current system, power associated with the periodic exchange of energy in electric and magnetic fields rather than net energy consumption, measured in volt-amperes reactive.
In elementary physics, a quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as displacement, velocity, or force.
A sequence of three nucleotides in a transfer RNA molecule that pairs with a complementary codon in messenger RNA during protein synthesis.
A deceptive scheme intended to obtain another person's money, property, or sensitive information.
In cricket, dismissal when a legal delivery hits the batter's body before the bat and would have hit the wicket, provided the pitching, impact, and shot-attempt conditions in the law are satisfied.
The recording of a baby's heart rate and uterine contractions during pregnancy or labour to assess the baby's wellbeing.
An artificial device that replaces a missing body part.
An adjustment to business income that removes inventory holding gains or losses caused by price changes, so that measured profits reflect current production.
In surgery, the use of high-frequency electric current to heat tissue for cutting, destroying tissue, or controlling bleeding.
An algorithmic method that solves overlapping subproblems and stores their results so that each need not be solved repeatedly.
In national economic accounts, tangible products that can be stored and have an average useful life of less than three years.
The selection or adjustment of a mathematical function so that its curve approximates a set of observed data points.
A search method that checks items one at a time until the target is found or all items have been examined.
The study of friction, wear, and lubrication between surfaces in relative motion.
In coordination chemistry, an atom, ion, or molecule that binds to a central atom or ion to form a coordination complex.
A control system that uses feedback from its output to compare actual and desired behaviour and adjust its action.
The study and design of interactions between people and their tasks, tools, and environments to improve wellbeing and system performance.
A mathematical structure consisting of vertices and edges that represent connections between vertices.
The observable characteristics of an organism, arising from its genetic constitution and environmental influences.
Electric current that flows in one direction, even if its magnitude varies with time.
Numerical vector representations of data items learned or constructed so that useful relationships between items are reflected in the vectors.
Loss of sensation induced for a medical procedure, affecting part or all of the body and sometimes accompanied by loss of consciousness.
A state of reduced activity and metabolism that helps certain animals survive hot or dry conditions.
A coil of wire, usually wound in a cylindrical form, that produces a magnetic field when electric current flows through it.
A thermodynamic state quantity equal to a system's internal energy plus the product of its pressure and volume: H = U + pV.
The use of computational and statistical methods to discover useful patterns, relationships, or structures in data.
A data structure that supports adding items and accessing or removing the item with the highest priority, according to an ordering assigned to the items.
An individual picture element in a digital image or display, represented by a colour or intensity value.
The electricity actually generated during a period divided by the electricity that would have been generated by continuous operation at full capacity throughout that period.
The Earth's magnetic field and the scientific study of its origin, properties, and changes.
The change of a liquid into vapour at its surface.
A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway and is regenerated overall rather than consumed by the reaction.
The identification of a disease or condition from symptoms, examination findings, and test results.
The complex of DNA and associated proteins that packages genetic material into chromosomes in eukaryotic cells.
An immune response to a substance that is normally harmless, producing symptoms in a person who is sensitive to it.
In cricket, a delivery pitched close to the batter's feet or the base of the stumps.
A localised wave that maintains its shape and speed through a balance of nonlinear and dispersive effects and recovers its form after interactions with other such waves.
A quantum of a collective vibrational mode in a material, such as the lattice vibrations of a crystal.
Payments by corporations to shareholders in cash or other assets, excluding distributions of the corporation's own shares.
In this energy-statistics context, liquid fuels and blending components produced from biomass, used mainly for transport.
A line on a map joining locations with equal temperature.

In association football, an offence involving active play from an offside position when a teammate plays or touches the ball. The position is in the opponents' half, nearer their goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent, with specified exceptions.
A change in the observed frequency of a wave caused by relative motion between its source and observer.
A tree data structure in which each node has at most two children.
A device that supplies controlled electrical energy to replenish a rechargeable battery.
A system of exchanging goods or services directly for other goods or services without using money as the medium of exchange.
A sorting algorithm that divides a sequence into parts, recursively sorts each part, and merges the sorted parts into one ordered sequence.
A meeting or class in which participants study or discuss a specific topic, often through presentations and guided discussion.
Software that displays advertisements, sometimes by collecting information about a user's activity or showing unwanted advertising.
An algorithmic strategy that divides a problem into smaller instances, solves them, often recursively, and combines their results to solve the original problem.
An instrument used to measure humidity, the amount of water vapour in air.

A thermodynamic state quantity related to the number and probabilities of accessible microscopic states. For a reversible change at constant temperature, its change equals the transferred heat divided by absolute temperature.
One of the two copies of a replicated chromosome, initially joined to its sister copy at the centromere.
The scientific study of climate, including its long-term patterns, variability, and causes.
Testing people without symptoms to identify possible disease or increased risk, so that further assessment or treatment can be offered.
An insulating material that retains a persistent electric polarisation or trapped electric charge.
The study and practice of flight through the atmosphere, including the design and operation of aircraft.
A dry copying or printing process that uses an electrically charged light-sensitive surface to form a toner image and transfer it to paper or another material.

tasks.concept: Net exports of goods and services
tasks.definition: The value of an economy's exports of goods and services minus its imports of goods and services.
Treatment that supplies hormones to replace those the body no longer produces in sufficient amounts.
A hardware or software security mechanism that permits or blocks network traffic according to specified rules.
The decline in the value of fixed assets used in production over an accounting period because of wear, obsolescence, ageing, and accidental damage.
A price index comparing the cost of a fixed basket at current prices with its cost at base-period prices, using base-period quantities as weights.
An electron tube that generates microwaves using the interaction of electrons with electric and magnetic fields oriented across one another.
A broadcasting service that transmits coded text and simple graphics for users to select and display as pages on a suitably equipped television.
A control system that acts on an input or command without using feedback from its output to correct its action.
In electronics, a circuit that uses a power supply to generate a repeating electrical waveform without a repeating external input signal.
A discredited set of beliefs and practices claiming that selective human reproduction can improve the inherited characteristics of future generations.
The forced upward movement of air as it encounters hills or mountains, which can lead to cooling, cloud formation, and precipitation.
A technique that records the interference of light waves and uses the resulting pattern to reconstruct an object's light field, producing a three-dimensional appearance.
Government grants to private businesses or government enterprises that support their production activities.
A small electronic device worn in or behind the ear that processes and amplifies sound to help a person with hearing loss.
An aircraft whose powered rotating blades provide lift and allow hovering and vertical take-off and landing.
A chromosome other than a sex chromosome.
An optical instrument with two aligned telescopes, one for each eye, that magnifies distant objects.
The record of transactions between residents and nonresidents in goods, services, primary income, and current transfers over an accounting period.
Phishing carried out through telephone calls or other voice communication.
A collection in which items are added and removed at one end, so the most recently added item is removed first: last in, first out.
Radiant energy from the Sun that can be converted into heat, electricity, or other useful forms of energy.
The deliberate eating of soil, earth, or clay by a human or other animal.
A surgical incision through the abdominal wall to examine or operate on organs inside the abdomen.
The process of calculating and paying employees' wages or salaries, including applicable deductions and related records.
In a single-phase alternating-current circuit, the product of root-mean-square voltage and current, measured in volt-amperes; it combines the effects of active and reactive power.
Weather radar that uses frequency changes in reflected radio waves to measure the component of a target's velocity towards or away from the radar.
In national economic accounts, tangible products that can be stored and have an average useful life of at least three years.
A price measure equal to the current-price value of an aggregate divided by its corresponding constant-price or chained-volume value, multiplied by 100.
A naturally occurring gaseous mixture composed mainly of methane, commonly used as a fuel.
A digital image capturing what is displayed on all or part of a screen at a particular time.
A wing-like surface that generates lift as it moves through water, used to raise a vessel's hull or a board above the water surface.
A mechanism that transmits rotary motion and power between shafts using a flexible belt running over pulleys.
Drug-induced relaxation and reduced awareness used to help a person tolerate a medical procedure; its depth can range from mild drowsiness to deep sedation.
In cricket, dismissal when the fielding side fairly puts down a wicket while the ball is in play and a batter is outside their ground, subject to the laws' exceptions.
Describing an organism that obtains its carbon from organic compounds made by other organisms rather than fixing inorganic carbon itself.
In boxing, an illegal punch that lands below the opponent's belt line.
The theft of payment-card data by secretly capturing information from a card, often using a device attached to a cash machine or payment terminal.
A network of physical objects equipped with sensors, software, or other technology that enables them to collect and exchange data over communication networks.
The study of how health-related conditions and events are distributed in populations, what determines them, and how this knowledge can help control health problems.
An instrument that indicates altitude relative to a reference level, commonly by measuring atmospheric pressure.
The removal of cells or tissue from the body for examination to help diagnose disease.
An activity in which people sing to recorded musical accompaniment while following displayed lyrics.
A vector quantity describing local rotation in a fluid, defined as the curl of the fluid's velocity field.
A hypothetical thin, extremely dense, line-like defect in space that may have formed during symmetry-breaking transitions in the early universe.
Energy carried by electromagnetic radiation, such as visible light, infrared radiation, or radio waves.
A power-generation system in which hot exhaust from a gas turbine is used to produce steam that drives a steam turbine, generating additional electricity.
An organism's genetic constitution, referring either to the variants at a particular genomic location or to a broader set of genetic variants.
Electric current that periodically reverses direction.
An arrangement in which a third party holds money, property, or documents until agreed conditions for their release have been met.
Non-fossil organic material from plants, animals, or other biological sources that can be used as an energy source.
In the EIA operating-reserve definition used here, unused available generating capability at peak load expressed as a percentage of total capability.
A DNA sequence that can move or copy itself to a different position within a genome.
On-demand network access to shared computing resources, such as servers, storage, and applications, that can be provisioned and released as needed.
Programs and associated instructions or data that direct a computer to perform tasks.
In online communication, an image, video, phrase, or other recognisable item that spreads between users, often through imitation and variation.
A self-employed person who undertakes work for clients on a project or contract basis.
The rate at which atmospheric temperature changes with height, conventionally positive when temperature decreases with increasing altitude.
A quantitative analytical method in which a measured amount of a reagent is added until a defined endpoint is reached, allowing the amount or concentration of another substance to be determined.
An instrument that produces brief, repeated flashes of light so that periodic motion can appear stationary or slowed and its frequency can be measured.
An unwanted secondary image produced in an optical system, often by internal reflections.
In meteorology, the horizontal transport of air or atmospheric properties, such as heat or moisture, by moving air.
Software intentionally designed to damage or disrupt systems, steal information, or perform other unauthorised actions.
The use of techniques such as X-rays, ultrasound, or magnetic resonance to produce images of structures or processes inside the body for medical assessment.
The measurement of heat transferred during a physical, chemical, or biological process.
Software tools that conceal malicious activity or privileged unauthorised access on a computer system.
The measurement of electromagnetic radiation in terms of physical quantities such as radiant energy and power, rather than perceived brightness.
A state of certain materials below a critical temperature in which electrical resistance vanishes and magnetic behaviour changes; it persists only within limits on current and magnetic field.
A binary tree organised so that keys in each node's left subtree are smaller than its key and keys in its right subtree are larger, allowing ordered searching.
A metallic material composed of two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal.
The scientific study of animal behaviour.
Goods and services supplied by residents of an economy to nonresidents.
In boxing, a result in which a boxer loses because they cannot resume the contest after a knockdown, normally within the referee's count.

In association football, a restart awarded for certain offences by a defending player in their own penalty area, in which a player kicks from the penalty mark with only the opposing goalkeeper defending the goal.
The automatic measurement and transmission of data from a remote location to a receiving system for monitoring or analysis.
Spending to acquire, add to, or improve property, plant, and equipment, including construction and qualifying exploration and development costs.
A chromosome region at which the kinetochore forms, enabling spindle fibres to attach and chromosomes to be separated during cell division.
The exchange of corresponding DNA segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during meiosis, producing new combinations of alleles.
A network device that forwards data packets between different networks using destination addresses and routing information.
The combination of multiple signals or data streams for transmission over a shared communication channel, with provision for separating them at the receiving end.
A cheque issued to an employee as payment of wages or salary.

In association football, a restart awarded to a team after an offence by its opponents; it may be direct, allowing a goal without another touch, or indirect, requiring another player's touch before a goal can count.
An automatic control system that maintains or changes an aircraft's flight path or attitude according to selected commands.
An instrument that measures the total electric charge passed through a circuit, often using an electrochemical reaction.
A hospital unit providing continuous monitoring and specialised treatment for critically ill patients.
An ultrasound technique that uses changes in the frequency of reflected sound to assess blood flow through vessels.
The glands and other hormone-producing organs that release hormones into the blood to regulate functions elsewhere in the body.
A graph traversal method that explores a path as far as possible before backtracking to explore other paths.
A doctor who specialises in diagnosing and treating disorders of the blood and blood-forming tissues.
An instrument that measures wind speed.
A segment of a gene's RNA transcript that is retained after splicing in the mature RNA; it may or may not encode part of a protein.
An algorithm that builds a solution by repeatedly making the best available local choice, without necessarily obtaining the best overall solution.
A stop at an intermediate airport between flights on the same journey.
The value of final goods and services produced within an economy during a specified period, equivalently the sum of value added in production.
A data structure that uses a hash function to map keys to storage locations for efficient insertion, lookup, and deletion, with a method for handling collisions.
A large atmospheric circulation around a region of high pressure, with clockwise flow in the Northern Hemisphere and anticlockwise flow in the Southern Hemisphere.
A power plant in which hot gases produced by fuel combustion expand through a gas turbine to drive an electrical generator.
A substance or molecular structure specifically recognised by antibodies or immune-cell receptors; it may originate outside the body or from the body's own cells.
An employer-initiated loss or suspension of employment because of business conditions or organisational needs rather than individual misconduct.
The study of control and communication in systems, including how feedback regulates the behaviour of machines and living organisms.
A physical separation method in which mixture components distribute between a stationary phase and a mobile phase that moves in a definite direction.
A person or institution responsible for safeguarding financial assets on behalf of their owners.
The introduction of air into a liquid or material, for example to increase dissolved oxygen in water or improve air circulation in soil.
A device in a spark-ignition engine that mixes fuel with incoming air in proportions suitable for combustion.
Assets such as deposits, shares, bonds, and loans that represent financial claims or ownership interests and have economic value.
A mobile telephone with an operating system that supports applications, internet access, and other computing functions.
An input device that optically captures a document or image and converts it into digital data.
A sequence of three nucleotides in DNA or messenger RNA that specifies an amino acid or a stop signal during protein synthesis.
A technique or system that uses sound to detect or locate underwater objects, either by listening to sounds or by transmitting sound and receiving its echoes.
A seminar or presentation delivered over the internet, often allowing participants to ask questions or interact with the presenter.
In fluid dynamics, a measure of the linkage and twisting of vortex lines, calculated as the volume integral of fluid velocity dotted with vorticity.
The synthesis and release of hormones by specialised nerve cells.
The processing of RNA from one gene by joining its exons in different combinations, producing different mature RNA transcripts and potentially different proteins.
The presence of extra or missing individual chromosomes in a cell, rather than a change involving complete chromosome sets.
A vehicle supported above a surface by a cushion of pressurised air, allowing travel over water or relatively level ground.
An input device with a movable stick whose direction or position controls movement or other actions in a computer, game, or machine.
The person whose life or life expectancy is used to determine payments under an annuity contract; this person may differ from the contract owner.
The science and practice of measuring time and designing, making, and maintaining timekeeping instruments.
The field concerned with designing, building, programming, and operating programmable machines that perform physical tasks automatically or under human control.
The value of production attributable to labour and property supplied by an economy's residents, regardless of where that production takes place.
A balloon-carried instrument that transmits measurements of atmospheric temperature, humidity, and pressure; tracking its position also provides wind speed and direction.
Phishing carried out through text messages, typically to obtain sensitive information or induce an unsafe action.
A deliberate attempt to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of a computer system, network, or its information.
In an electric drive, slowing a motor by making it act as a generator and dissipating the generated electrical energy as heat in a braking resistor.
A temporary work placement intended to provide practical experience and learning in a field or organisation.
A graph traversal method that explores vertices in successive levels of distance, measured in edges, from a starting vertex.

The study of changes in gene activity associated with chemical or structural modifications of DNA and chromatin, without changes to the underlying DNA sequence; some such changes persist through cell division.
The binding of two or more separate sites on the same ligand to one central atom, usually a metal atom or ion, forming a chelate.
Stitches used to hold together the edges of a wound or surgical incision while it heals.
The temperature to which air must be cooled, at constant pressure and water-vapour content, to become saturated with respect to liquid water.
A pictorial character used in digital communication to represent an emotion, object, activity, or idea.
A photograph that a person takes of themselves, usually using a smartphone or digital camera.
A substance that lowers surface or interfacial tension by concentrating at the boundary between phases, such as water and air or water and oil.
An interconnected system of electricity generators, transmission and distribution lines, and associated equipment that supplies electricity to users.
